Latin America.title: Keiko Fujimori wins Peru's presidency as the full count confirms her by 49,641 votes
Latin America.summary: Peru's National Office of Electoral Processes (ONPE) on Monday closed the count of the presidential runoff at 100% of the tally sheets and confirmed the victory of right-wing Keiko Fujimori over left-wing Roberto Sánchez, 22 days after the June 7 vote. The Fuerza Popular leader obtained 50.14% of valid votes against her rival's 49.87%, a difference of 49,641 ballots, in one of the closest elections in the country's recent history.

Latin America.title: Paraguay declares a holiday after reaching the World Cup's last 16 by beating Germany
Latin America.summary: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña declared a national holiday for Tuesday, June 30, to celebrate the national team's qualification for the round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, after eliminating Germany in a penalty shootout. "Today a whole country is celebrating," the president wrote on the social network X, where he published the decree and congratulated the team, which he called by its nickname, the Albirroja.

Latin America.title: A regional shift to the right frames the wave of congratulations to Fujimori
Latin America.summary: The confirmation of right-wing Keiko Fujimori's victory in Peru's presidential runoff drew a wave of congratulations from leaders across the region, who framed the result within the shift to the right underway in several Latin American countries. With Fujimori's arrival in power, the right will add a new government, alongside those of Argentina, Ecuador, Chile, Paraguay and El Salvador, and the recent victory of Abelardo de la Espriella in Colombia.

Latin America.title: Argentina taps the local market to fund a $4.2 billion bondholder payment due July 9

Latin America.title: Venezuela's María Corina Machado accuses the government of blocking her return after the earthquake

Latin America.title: Mexican rescuers in Venezuela call it one of the largest tragedies they have faced

Latin America.title: Argentina's Pacific-pact bid would make it a trade partner of the UK, raising a Falklands dilemma
